hook_text: For three months, more people returned the AI Pin than bought one.
full_transcript: For three months, more people returned the AI Pin than bought one. Humane pitched a six hundred ninety-nine dollar lapel pin designed to replace the smartphone. They shipped about ten thousand units, pulling in roughly nine million dollars. Then net sales went negative. Between May and August 2024, daily returns consistently surpassed new orders. Over one million dollars in hardware bounced back to their warehouse. Worse, Humane could not resell the returned devices. Because of T-Mobile carrier locking constraints, they could not wipe and reassign the internal cellular chips. Thousands of returned pins turned directly into e-waste. By August, active users dropped below seven thousand. In February 2025, HP bought Humane's software assets for one hundred and sixteen million dollars, ditching the hardware entirely. On February twenty-eighth, the cloud servers shut down. Every pin bricked instantly. That is six hundred ninety-nine dollars for a silent metal badge.
